## Purpose

This SOP describes the estimation of soil organic matter (SOM) content using the loss-on-ignition (LOI) method. SOM is quantified by measuring the mass lost when oven-dried soil is combusted at 550 C in a muffle furnace.


## Scope

- **Applies to:** Air-dried, sieved soil samples collected per SOP-F02
- **Does not apply to:** Soils with high calcium carbonate content (CaCO~3~ decomposes above 450 C and may inflate LOI values; consider an alternative method such as Walkley-Black or elemental analysis for calcareous soils)
- **Location:** EA Program laboratory, SGM 133


## Responsibilities

| Role              | Responsibility                                          |
|:------------------|:--------------------------------------------------------|
| Lab PI            | Approve protocol, ensure training compliance            |
| Trained Personnel | Perform analysis, record and report results             |
| New Students      | Complete training before independent use                |


## Safety and Hazards

::: {.callout-warning}
### Hazards

- **Physical:** Muffle furnace operates at 550 C; severe burn risk. Drying oven at 105 C. Ceramic crucibles remain extremely hot after removal.
- **Chemical:** None (no reagents used)
:::

### Required PPE

- [ ] Heat-resistant gloves (when handling crucibles from furnace or oven)
- [ ] Safety glasses
- [ ] Lab coat
- [ ] Closed-toed shoes


## Equipment and Materials

| Item                          | Notes                                        |
|:------------------------------|:---------------------------------------------|
| Muffle furnace                | Capable of sustained 550 C                   |
| Drying oven                   | Set to 105 C                                 |
| Ceramic crucibles             | Pre-combusted; labeled or numbered           |
| Analytical balance            | 0.0001 g (0.1 mg) resolution                |
| Desiccator with desiccant     | For cooling crucibles before weighing        |
| Metal tongs or crucible tongs | Heat-resistant, for handling hot crucibles    |
| Spatula                       | For transferring soil to crucibles           |


## Procedure

### Crucible Preparation

1. Pre-combust all ceramic crucibles in the muffle furnace at 550 C for 1 hour to remove any residual organic material
2. Cool crucibles in a desiccator to room temperature
3. Weigh each empty crucible to the nearest 0.0001 g and record as $W_{\text{crucible}}$

### Drying at 105 C

1. Add approximately 5 g of air-dried, sieved (2 mm) soil to a pre-weighed crucible
2. Record the exact mass of crucible + soil
3. Place crucibles in the drying oven at 105 C for 24 hours
4. Remove crucibles, cool in a desiccator, and weigh to the nearest 0.0001 g
5. Record as $W_{105}$ (mass of oven-dried soil, excluding crucible)

::: {.callout-tip}
### Tip
If the mass has not stabilized (i.e., decreases by more than 0.001 g on re-weighing), return the sample to the oven for an additional 2--4 hours and re-weigh.
:::

### Combustion at 550 C

1. Transfer the crucibles containing oven-dried soil directly into the muffle furnace
2. Ramp the furnace to 550 C (if programmable, use a ramp rate of approximately 10 C per minute)
3. Hold at 550 C for 4 hours
4. Turn off the furnace and allow crucibles to cool inside the furnace until they can be safely transferred (below approximately 200 C)
5. Transfer crucibles to a desiccator and cool to room temperature
6. Weigh to the nearest 0.0001 g
7. Record as $W_{550}$ (mass of combusted soil, excluding crucible)

### Calculation

Soil organic matter content is calculated as:

$$
\text{SOM (\%)} = \left( \frac{W_{105} - W_{550}}{W_{105}} \right) \times 100
$$

where:

- $W_{105}$ = mass of oven-dried soil (g)
- $W_{550}$ = mass of soil after combustion at 550 C (g)


## Quality Control

- Run analytical duplicates for at least 10% of samples; coefficient of variation should be less than 5%
- Include an empty crucible blank in each furnace run to verify no mass gain from ambient contamination
- Include a laboratory reference soil with known SOM in each batch
- Verify oven (105 C) and furnace (550 C) temperatures using a calibrated thermometer or thermocouple at regular intervals


## Waste Disposal

| Waste Type              | Disposal Method                             |
|:------------------------|:--------------------------------------------|
| Combusted soil residue  | Standard trash (inert mineral ash)          |
| Crucibles               | Clean and reuse                             |


## References

- Nelson, D.W. & Sommers, L.E. (1996). Total carbon, organic carbon, and organic matter. In: Sparks, D.L. (Ed.), *Methods of Soil Analysis, Part 3: Chemical Methods*. SSSA Book Series No. 5, pp. 961--1010.
- Heiri, O., Lotter, A.F., & Lemcke, G. (2001). Loss on ignition as a method for estimating organic and carbonate content in sediments: reproducibility and comparability of results. *Journal of Paleolimnology*, 25, 101--110.


## Training Record

Before performing this procedure independently, personnel must:

1. Read this SOP in full
2. Demonstrate safe operation of the muffle furnace and drying oven
3. Demonstrate proper use of the analytical balance and desiccator
4. Perform the procedure under supervision with acceptable duplicate precision
5. Be signed off by the PI or lab manager
